svg.title: Reading the Na₂SO₄–H₂O enthalpy–concentration chart (Foust Fig. 19.28)
svg.text: Reading the Na₂SO₄–H₂O enthalpy–concentration chart (Foust Fig. 19.28)
Bases: H = 0 for liquid water at 32 °F and for solid Na₂SO₄ at 32 °F; 1 atm. Approximate redraw.
Feed: 20 % at 200 °F. Go up from 20 % to the 200 °F isotherm (one-phase region), across: h_F ≈ 136 Btu/lb.
Saturated mother liquor at 60 °F: the 60 °F isotherm ends on the decahydrate solubility curve at 12.2 %: h_ML ≈ 21.
Crystals Na₂SO₄·10H₂O at 60 °F: the other end of the 60 °F tie line, at 44.1 %: h_C ≈ −82 Btu/lb.
The 60 °F tie line joins the two phases of the magma; the overall magma point (23.2 %) lies on it (lever rule).
Approximate redraw of the attached chart (straight isotherms through its key points); in the exam read the printed chart.
